children: traded higher on Thursday after the Israeli biotech said that it maintains an adequate supply of KedRAB, its human immune globulin targeting rabies, even as cases linked to the viral disease are rising in the U.S.
Last week, issuing a health advisory, the CDC reported a significant increase in human rabies exposures and the use of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis.

According to the agency, there was a 17% increase in rabies-related inquiries from July through August and a 76% rise in the utilization of two U.S.-licensed rabies immunoglobulins for the week ending Sept. 2.
“In light of this increase in end-user utilization described in the CDC advisory, Kamada confirms it has the inventory and manufacturing capacity to support the continued supply of KedRAB,”
